content:
maya: Heads-up — ran a perf job on 8xA100 with the latest graph-replay changes and saw comm/compute overlap collapse for the MLP-heavy microbench.
maya: nvtx/timeline shows NCCL all-reduce happening strictly after each GEMM instead of concurrently.
liam: ugh, saw something similar locally. Any chance this is the cuda-graph handshake change from last week?
reza: Can you paste the timeline snippet?
maya: Sure. From CUPTI timeline (simplified):
```
0.000ms  kernel: gemm_kern (gpu0)
1.2ms   cudaGraph capture_end (gpu0)
1.2ms   cudaEvent record (host -> gpu0)
1.3ms   nccl: allreduce (gpu0)
1.3ms   nccl: allreduce (gpu1)
1.3ms   kernel: gemm_kern (gpu1)
```
maya: Notice the 1.2ms host/handshake gap during capture that forces serial ordering of nccl after the preceding gemm. This repeats per micro-batch.
sasha: That host-side handshake sounds like the capture->replay synchronization we added to ensure NVTX ordering for profiling, right?
liam: We added a synchronous stream drain when capturing mixed stream workloads (to avoid lost memcpys). It might be introducing an extra host-sync event that breaks overlap.
reza: Also saw the kernel selector fallback on some ranks: small batch sizes trigger the 'small-matmul' slower kernel on GPU1 but not GPU0, so compute durations vary — that can widen handshakes and make NCCL wait.
perf-bot: perf/regression alert: 7.8x higher end-to-end latency for small-batch MLP benchmark (8xA100, tp=4, pp=2) vs baseline.
opsbot: link to job: https://ci.internal/runs/2188
liam: Two hypotheses: 1) the capture handshake inserted a host-synced event that serializes capture+nccl, 2) kernel selection variance + batching heuristics amplify skew between ranks so allreduce can't overlap.
maya: I profiled per-rank durations — attached small table:
```
rank0 compute: 1.0ms, nccl start: 1.05ms
rank1 compute: 1.4ms, nccl start: 1.42ms
rank2 compute: 1.02ms, nccl start: 1.06ms
```
maya: The longer compute on rank1 pushes its nccl to start later, but the capture handshake adds ~0.2-0.3ms that aligns nccl starts across ranks, making them serialize.
sasha: Do we have code changes that moved NCCL launch onto the capture stream instead of a comm stream? I remember a refactor.
reza: Yeah, recent change funnels all kernel launches into the graph capture stream for determinism. But that means NCCL launches are ordered with respect to capture_end on each device; host-side event ordering can make them line up rather than naturally stagger and overlap.
liam: Quick mitigation options:
- revert NCCL launches to comm stream outside capture (risking missing captured ops)
- change handshake to use device->device event instead of host sync (cudaEventRecord + cudaStreamWaitEvent on peer streams)
- add tiny jitter/async pre-warm to reduce rank skew and force natural staggering
- improve kernel selection to reduce compute variance across ranks
m aya: I ran a small experiment: replaced host sync with device-side event + streamWaitEvent. Overlap restored on a small repro. Timeline snippet:
```
0.000ms kernel: gemm_kern (gpu0)
0.000ms kernel: gemm_kern (gpu1)
1.05ms nccl: allreduce (gpu0)
1.10ms nccl: allreduce (gpu1)
```
reza: Nice. That suggests the host round-trip was the main culprit. But we still need to address kernel selection skew and batching.
sasha: About batching heuristics — for this workload autoprefetch chooses micro-batch size 1 occasionally because per-token latency budget is tiny. That increases number of allreduces and reduces per-reduce size, raising relative NCCL overhead.
liam: Right. For small micro-batches, kernel chooser sometimes picks the 'generic' matmul for GPU1 due to heuristic threshold boundaries. We should smooth thresholds or pick consistent kernel across identical model shards to avoid rank-to-rank timing divergence.
maya: Proposed action items:
- Rework capture handshake to use device events (PR draft up) — owner: maya — ETA: today
- Add a short async KV pre-warm on graph init to eliminate the first-capture host sync path — owner: reza — ETA: 2 days
- Tweak kernel selection thresholds to bias toward the faster 'large' kernel when within 10% perf difference to avoid rank skew — owner: liam — ETA: 1 week
- Add a test in perf infra that runs multi-rank micro-batch workloads and asserts overlap ratio > 0.6 — owner: sasha — ETA: 1 week

sasha: One more: add a debug nvtx marker around nccl launches describing chosen kernel variant and batch size so we can correlate in timeline.
reza: Agree. Also log whether we're in capture path vs direct launch in the nccl wrapper.
liam: I'll open the kernel-selector PR to smooth boundary and add a forced-consistency mode for multi-gpu runs.
perf-bot: note: the regression alert will stay until overlap >= 0.6 on the benchmark.
maya: I'll push the device-event handshake PR now and kick a gated perf run. If that fixes 90% of the issue we can upstream the rest as follow-ups.
liam: Thanks — ping me if you want me to bisect the kernel selector changes.
maya: pinging @sasha once result is in.
